findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “The back side of the desert…”
findings.source_quote: The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “zealot” as “yweraar” or equivalent, not “ywerige mens”; preserve the contrast between too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh.
findings.translation_quote: Die ondergang van die ywerige mens is dikwels te min vertroue in God en te veel vertroue in die vlees.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “The miraculous river rescue…”
findings.source_quote: The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter
findings.suggested_fix: Change “filistin” to “Farao se dogter” (or the conventional Afrikaans equivalent).
findings.translation_quote: Die wonderlike redding uit die rivier deur die filistin se dogter

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “For us, it represents…”
findings.source_quote: we can have a lapse in faith
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “afasie” with “’n geloofsverslapping” or another expression meaning a lapse in faith.
findings.translation_quote: ons ’n afasie in geloof kan hê

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “For us, it represents…”
findings.source_quote: our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the image as prayers seeming to hit the ceiling and bounce back, while preserving the personification that they mockingly tell us our usefulness in God’s Kingdom is over; remove “naaklach,” which does not convey “laughing.”
findings.translation_quote: ons gebede die plafon tref en terugkaats, wat naaklach en in gru-skarpery teen ons lieg dat ons bruikbaarheid in die Koninkryk van God verby is

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “For us, it represents…”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “tyding” with “tydsberekening” or “tydsberekening van God is volmaak,” so the sentence refers to God’s timing, not news.
findings.translation_quote: Maar God se tyding is perfek.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “En he trembling and astonished…”
findings.source_quote: Arise, and go into the city
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “Arise” as “Staan op” (or “Staan op en gaan na die stad”); “Staak op” does not mean “arise.”
findings.translation_quote: Staak op en gaan in die dorp

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “We learn from the account in Exodus…”
findings.source_quote: they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “accomplished by” as a process brought about by or achieved through; replace “berokken is deur,” which means it was inflicted by.
findings.translation_quote: hulle het deur die uitmergelende proses van skeiding van die vlees van die gees gegaan wat berokken is deur…

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “This doctrine was foreign to Egypt…”
findings.source_quote: This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “foreign to” as “vreemd aan” or “onbekend aan,” rather than “vreemdeling aan.”
findings.translation_quote: Hierdie leerstelling was vreemdeling aan Egipte en ook aan Moses.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “God has a purpose…”
findings.source_quote: the utter folly that his own hands had participated in
findings.suggested_fix: Translate “folly” as “dwaasheid” and preserve that Moses’s own hands had participated in it; “verbete dwaasheid” changes the meaning to stubborn or furious folly.
findings.translation_quote: die verbete dwaasheid waaraan sy eie hande deelgeneem het

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “Perhaps God is enamored…”
findings.source_quote: it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “stoel van oorwinning” with a phrase meaning “die punt van oorgawe/berusting”; the source describes resignation, not victory.
findings.translation_quote: die tyd wat dit geneem het vir Moses om by die stoel van oorwinning uit te kom

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “Not that Moses had attained perfection…”
findings.source_quote: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the printed quotation faithfully as an attempt to kill him, for example: “En op die pad, by die herberg, het die HERE hom ontmoet en probeer om hom dood te maak – Eksodus 4:24.”
findings.translation_quote: En dit het gebeur onderweg in die herberg dat die HERE hom ontmoet en probeer het om hom te slaan dood – Eksodus 4:24.

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “Not that Moses had attained perfection…”
findings.source_quote: the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14
findings.suggested_fix: Use the conventional Afrikaans rendering of the quoted name, “EK IS WAT EK IS,” and retain the reference to Eksodus 3:14.
findings.translation_quote: die groot EK IS WIE EK IS – sien Eksodus 3:14

findings.location: HTML, paragraph beginning “The rod is the power of God unto salvation…”
findings.source_quote: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace each occurrence of “teregstelling/teregstreep” in this quotation and its surrounding explanation with an Afrikaans term for chastening or discipline, such as “tugtiging/tugtig.” “Teregstelling” means execution and reverses the passage’s meaning. Retain Hebreërs 12:6-8.
findings.translation_quote: Dit is God se teregstelling. […] Want wie die Here liefhet, die teregstreep Hy, en wie Hy as ’n seun ontvang, die gesel Hy. As julle die teregstelling verdra […] watter seun is daar wat die vader nie teregstreep nie? Maar as julle sonder teregstelling is […] – Hebreërs 12:6-8.

findings.location: HTML, final paragraph before the figure
findings.source_quote: being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10
findings.suggested_fix: Use an idiomatic Afrikaans rendering of being conformed to Christ’s death, such as “aan sy dood gelykvormig te word”; retain Filippense 3:10.
findings.translation_quote: en dat ons na sy dood gevorm mag word – Filippense 3:10
